records.name: Friends of Wister Woods
records.summary: Neighbors who want the woods at Wister Woods Park kept clean, open and easy to walk. They held a litter cleanup in May 2023 and set goals for trails, invasive vines and litter, but we found no newer activity.
records.what_you_do: Litter cleanups around the park edges and the woods. The 2023 goals include a looped trail and clearing invasive vines.

first_step.how: Email Parks and Recreation's stewardship office (pprstewardship@phila.gov) and ask to be connected with this Friends group

records.notes: Status is dormant because the newest evidence is a May 2023 profile, which is more than 24 months old. The profile says the group is part of the Park Friends Network. No website, social link or contact for the group was published. The City list email is the stewardship office, so it is not used. A bird walk at the picnic area listed for October 5, 2025 (dvoc.org) does not mention this group, so it is not used as evidence.

records.name: Friends of Dickinson Square Park
records.summary: Neighbors who care for John Dickinson Square Park in South Philadelphia. A Tree Team waters young trees each week, a gardening committee tends the park, and a parents' committee works with families.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for a weekly watering shift of about 45 minutes (training is provided), join the gardening committee, or join the parents' committee.

schedule.text: Tree Team watering is a flexible weekly shift of about 45 minutes, signed up through the group's form

first_step.how: Sign up on the Tree Team form at dickinsonsquarepark.org for a weekly watering shift
first_step.basis: The site says training is provided and gives a sign-up form for new volunteers.

records.notes: Status is probably_active because the group's own site is working and current in form but shows no dated events or news. The email on the site is for the Gardening Committee. The City list gives dickinsonsqpark@gmail.com as the group's address; it was not confirmed on the site, so it is not used. The newsletter sign-up page has no dated issues either. Social links were recorded from the site, not read.

records.what_you_do: We have not confirmed what this group does.

first_step.how: Email neighborsgardenphilly@gmail.com, the address the City lists for this group, and ask how to join the garden

records.notes: One search and one 2026 City article about Hatfield House found nothing about a garden group there. The category gardening-greening comes from the name only. The email comes from the City list alone and was not confirmed on any other page, so check it before relying on it. records.name: Philadelphia Grotto
records.summary: A local caving club, a chapter of the National Speleological Society, that works on cave conservation, exploration and education. New people start by coming to a monthly meeting, and beginners go caving with experienced leaders.
records.what_you_do: Come to the monthly meeting, learn caving gear and safety, and join trips led by experienced cavers. Members also help with cave conservation.

schedule.text: Monthly meeting on the first Thursday of the month, 7:30 to 9:30 pm for the October meeting (the page gives no year)

locations.label: Monthly meetings at a member's home in Media, PA, or online

first_step.how: Come to the first-Thursday monthly meeting (the meeting link is posted on phillygrotto.org) and ask for the membership form
first_step.basis: The New Cavers page says newcomers attend a monthly meeting, receive a membership form, and cave with experienced leaders.

records.notes: Status is probably_active. The meeting page lists an October 1st meeting but gives no year. October 1 falls on a Thursday in 2026, which fits, but the page does not state the year. The homepage shows no dated news. The meeting place is a member's home, so only the town and zip are published. The club's address on the NSS listing is the same home, so it is left out. Chartered 1947, per the club's site. The contact is a comment form only, so no email is recorded. Media is outside the city limits; the club is included because its name and monthly meetings are Philadelphia area. The owner may want to review suburban clubs together (see Bucks County Grotto). The New Cavers page is at /new-members/; the /new-cavers/ path returns 404.

records.name: Bald Eagle Grotto
records.notes: Based in Cogan Station, central Pennsylvania. Meets by Zoom on the second Wednesday at 7 pm, open to anyone interested, so a Philadelphia caver could join online. Not listed as a Philadelphia group. The owner may want to decide whether online-only clubs belong in the directory. The page gives a 2026 nonprofit year without a month.

records.name: Bucks County Grotto
records.notes: Address is Warrington, Bucks County, a suburb north of the city. The page names no service area or meeting place and gives no newcomer steps, so it is not counted as a Philadelphia group. This is a judgment call: if the owner wants suburban clubs listed, review this one together with Philadelphia Grotto, which meets in Media.
